tagline: From Port Royal to the island’s changing ground.
intro: From Port Royal, the McTeer Bridge spans the Beaufort River, over marshes and a marina, to Lady’s Island. The Broad River confluence lies to the south and the Beaufort waterfront to the north. Taller and wider than the old bridge from downtown, it came in the 1980s, as former plantation and timber tracts on the island turned into neighborhoods.

On the Port Royal side, Fort Frederick makes a separate excursion along the Beaufort River. Erosion has left part of the old fort underwater, while the heritage preserve keeps the surviving tabby walls beside the naval hospital.

moments.title: Fort Frederick Heritage Preserve
moments.text: The surviving tabby walls border the Beaufort River, which has eroded part of the old fort.

moments.title: Lady’s Island
moments.text: Beyond the crossing, a largely residential Sea Island includes upland forest, tidal water and freshwater wetlands.
